title: Rational polynomial additive-bar contraction
statement:
For a commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebra $B$ and an integer $r\geq0$, define the nonnegative cochain complex $P_{B,r}$ by
$$P_{B,r}^n=B[x_{a,i}:1\leq a\leq n,\ 1\leq i\leq r],\qquad n\geq0,$$
using polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Write $x_a=(x_{a,1},\ldots,x_{a,r})$. Its differential is
$$(df)(x_1,\ldots,x_{n+1})=f(x_2,\ldots,x_{n+1})+\sum_{a=1}^{n}(-1)^a f(x_1,\ldots,x_a+x_{a+1},\ldots,x_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(x_1,\ldots,x_n).$$
In degree zero the first and last terms cancel. Put $P^n=0$ for $n<0$.

Let $K_{B,r}^q$ be the free $B$-module on $e_I$ for subsets $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ of cardinality $q$, with zero differential and zero terms for $q<0$ or $q>r$. Define $i:K_{B,r}\to P_{B,r}$ by $i(e_\varnothing)=1$ and
$$i(e_{\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}})=x_{1,i_1}\cdots x_{q,i_q}.$$
Define $p^0=1_B$. For $q>0$, define $p^q$ on a polynomial monomial to be zero unless every block $x_a$ has total degree one and these degree-one coordinates have pairwise distinct indices $j_1,\ldots,j_q$. In that remaining case set
$$p^q(x_{1,j_1}\cdots x_{q,j_q})=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)e_{\{j_1,\ldots,j_q\}},$$
where $(j_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,j_{\sigma(q)})$ is increasingly ordered. Extend $B$-linearly. Then $d^2=0$, $di=0$, $pd=0$, $pi=1$, and there are $B$-linear maps $h^q:P_{B,r}^q\to P_{B,r}^{q-1}$ with
$$dh+hd=1-ip.$$
The maps $h$ can be chosen over $\mathbf Q$ and extended to every $B$: each rational monomial is sent to a finite rational linear combination of monomials, and all displayed identities hold after scalar extension. Thus this gives a chain homotopy equivalence, not only a list of cohomology groups. The zero algebra is allowed. For $r=0$, $i$ is the degree-zero inclusion of $B$ into the unnormalized constant cosimplicial complex.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-polynomial-bar-coface-retraction-identities] to the displayed $P,K,i,p$. It gives $d^2=0$, $di=0$, $pd=0$, $pi=1$, including degree zero, over every $B$. Give $e_I$ multidegree $1_I$; all these maps preserve multidegree.

source.place: Paragraph (3), algebraic obligation; assembly of Q59 re-split tasks, step 1

proof.text: Over $\mathbf Q$, [lem-sfb-polynomial-bar-divided-monomial-normalization] decomposes $P$ as the direct sum of the finite multidegree complexes $P_m$ and gives $P_m\simeq V_m^*$ by cochain homotopy equivalences, with the displayed adjacent-merge boundary on $V_m$. For a cocycle $z$, homotopic maps differ on $z$ by the boundary $dH(z)$; hence these equivalences induce inverse cohomology maps. Apply [lem-sfb-ordered-composition-complex-homology] to that exact boundary: $H^n(P_m)$ has dimension one precisely when $m$ is squarefree and $n=\sum_i m_i$, and vanishes otherwise. This includes $m=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), algebraic obligation; assembly of Q59 re-split tasks, step 2

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-polynomial-bar-coface-retraction-identities], the induced maps satisfy $p_*i_*=1$. In each multidegree and degree, $K_m^n$ and $H^n(P_m)$ have the same dimension, either zero or one, by the preceding step. A linear map between zero spaces is invertible; between one-dimensional spaces a map with a right inverse is invertible. Thus each $p_m$ is an isomorphism on cohomology, with inverse induced by the prescribed $i_m$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), algebraic obligation; assembly of Q59 re-split tasks, step 3

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-rational-based-retract-universal-homotopy] with $M=\mathbf N^r$, the monomial bases of $P_m$ and the subset bases of $K_m$. Its hypotheses are the identities and cohomology isomorphisms just established. It gives $m$-preserving rational $h$ on $\bigoplus_mP_m=P_{\mathbf Q,r}$ with $dh+hd=1-ip$, each column finitely supported. Its simultaneous matrix extension gives the desired identities over every $B$: the extended $d,i,p$ are exactly their stated monomial formulas. The zero algebra is included. When $r=0$, the differential parity is given by [lem-sfb-polynomial-bar-coface-retraction-identities] and the last clause of [lem-sfb-rational-based-retract-universal-homotopy] gives $h^n=1$ for even $n\geq2$ and zero otherwise. Extend by zero in negative degrees.
